title: Basics of Scientific Rigor and Reproducibility
audience: Basic science learners practicing transparent outlier handling
objectives: Visualize simulated eICU-style vital-sign data and identify outliers.
Calculate 1.5x IQR thresholds for outlier detection.
Compare summary statistics with and without outliers.
Evaluate remove, winsorize, and median-imputation strategies.
Reflect on transparent reporting for reproducibility.

sections.name: Dataset Overview
sections.how_to_use: Review heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and temperature values before selecting variables.

sections.name: Visualizing Outliers
sections.purpose: Use box plots to spot extreme values.
sections.how_to_use: Select a variable, inspect the box plot points, and note possible outlier patient IDs.

sections.name: Calculating Outlier Thresholds
sections.how_to_use: Choose a variable and review Q1, Q3, IQR, lower bound, upper bound, and flagged rows.

sections.name: Effect on Summary Statistics
sections.purpose: Show how outliers affect mean, standard deviation, and median.
sections.how_to_use: Compare all-data statistics against statistics after excluding IQR outliers.

sections.name: Handling Outliers
sections.how_to_use: Choose remove, winsorize, or median imputation and compare resulting summary statistics.

sections.name: Reflection
sections.purpose: Connect outlier handling to scientific rigor.
sections.how_to_use: Write what should be reported in methods for reproducibility.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner from visualization to IQR thresholds, statistics comparison, handling strategy, and reflection.
For basic science users, emphasize transparent reporting and how preprocessing choices affect conclusions.
Help learners interpret outliers without automatically assuming they are errors.
